events.system:
P = 4-(4-hydroxyphenyl)cyclohexan-1-one
P --[NaBH₄, C₂H₅OH]--> Q
Q --[SOCl₂, pyridine]--> R
R --[CH₃COCl, pyridine]--> S
S --[AgNO₂]--> T

events.hidden_link: Selective reduction of ketone over phenol by NaBH4 gives Q. SOCl2 substitutes the secondary alcohol with chlorine to give R. Acetyl chloride esterifies the phenolic OH to give S. AgNO2 yields the nitroalkane T (N-attack), while NaCN yields the nitrile U (C-attack).
events.route: 1. Identify P: ketone and phenol. NaBH4 reduces ketone to alcohol (Q). 2. SOCl2/pyridine converts the alcohol to chloride (R). 3. CH3COCl/pyridine acylates the phenol to an ester (S). 4. AgNO2 substitutes the chloride to form a nitro compound (T). 5. NaCN substitutes the chloride to form a nitrile (U).
events.student_must_notice: AgNO2 produces a nitro compound (T) rather than a nitrite, whereas NaCN produces a nitrile (U) rather than an isocyanide. Also, acylation in S removes the phenolic OH, making the FeCl3 test negative.
events.trap: Assuming AgNO2 forms a nitrite or NaCN forms an isocyanide, or forgetting that the phenol was acylated and predicting a positive FeCl3 test for S.
events.given: Reaction scheme and name of P
events.asked: Functional groups of T and U, and chemical tests for S and Q
events.why_hard: Requires precise knowledge of ambient nucleophile selectivity (AgNO2 vs NaNO2, NaCN vs AgCN) and tracking functional group transformations for chemical tests.

members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working: P is 4-(4-hydroxyphenyl)cyclohexan-1-one. NaBH4 in EtOH reduces ketone to alcohol giving Q = 4-(4-hydroxyphenyl)cyclohexan-1-ol. SOCl2/pyridine converts phenol OH to chloride giving R = 4-(4-chlorophenyl)cyclohexan-1-ol (phenol chloride). CH3COCl/pyridine acetylates phenol OH giving S = 4-(4-acetoxyphenyl)cyclohexan-1-ol (acetyl phenol). AgNO2 with S likely displaces acetoxy with nitrite? Actually AgNO2 can lead to nitrite substitution of acetoxy? But typical reaction of acyl chloride with AgNO2 gives nitro? No. However S is an acylated phenol; AgNO2 may lead to nitrite ester? Probably T is the nitrite ester (4-(4-nitrophenoxy)cyclohexan-1-ol) after substitution of acetoxy by nitrite? But AgNO2 with acylated phenol could give nitro? Likely T contains nitro? Unclear. U from NaCN on S gives nitrile? S has acetyl group; NaCN could displace acetyl with CN giving phenyl cyanide? Actually S has acetyl phenol; NaCN may give nitrile via substitution of acetyl? Probably U contains nitrile. V from NaI/acetone gives iodo compound. FeCl3 color with phenolic OH present in Q and S (if not acetylated). Q has phenol OH, gives FeCl3 color. S has acetoxy not phenol, no color. T may have nitro? unlikely. So correct: B (U nitrile) and D (Q FeCl3).

members.name: glm-5.3-flash
members.working: P has a free phenol and a ketone. NaBH4 reduces only the ketone to a secondary alcohol, so Q still has a free phenolic OH (gives violet color with neutral FeCl3 → D correct). SOCl2/pyridine converts the alcohol to chloride R (phenol still free). CH3COCl/pyridine acetylates the phenolic OH, giving S = aryl acetate with an alkyl chloride side chain; the phenol is now esterified, so S gives no FeCl3 coloration (C wrong). Alkyl chloride S reacts with AgNO2 to give the nitroalkane T (nitro group present → A correct), with NaCN to give the nitrile U (→ B correct), and with NaI (Finkelstein) to give iodide V.
